item.title: The Biggest Trump Retribution Scheme Is Coming Apart at the Seams
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Blanche Overpromises and UnderdeliversThe mother of all “investigate the investigators” retributions in south Florida suffered another major blow with the resignation of Kurt Olsen as its top prosecutor.Olsen’s departure marks the third top prosecutor in a row to leave the probe — though Olsen’s departure seems markedly different.A career prosecutor, Maria Medetis Long, left under duress in April, concerned that the case lacked evidence to proceed.Then Joseph diGenova — a Trump true believer — resigned under pressure earlier this month for not seeking indictments fast enough for Main Justice and the White House.Olsen, who took over after diGenova left, is even more of a true believer. He had worked on bogus election fraud cases while on the Trump II White House staff and had no prior prosecution experience before being assigned to the “grand conspiracy” case.And now he’s gone. Not just from the investigation, but from DOJ entirely.Olsen was also reportedly under pressure to produce indictments quickly, but he seems to have been undone by unspecified “issues with his security clearance” — a guffaw-worthy irony considering classified documents are at the center of the retributive investigation.Olsen’s supposed probe — predicated on the nonsense notion that Trump was the victim of a Deep State plot to deprive him of his civil rights — is especially focused on the indictment of Trump in the Mar-a-Lago classified documents case, so problems with his security clearance is a plot twist too implausible for a screenplay. Olsen’s resignation comes after FBI agents who investigated the Mar-a-Lago case were subpoenaed to testify before a grand jury overseen by U.S. District Judge Aileen Cannon — a development which spilled out into the open just last week.This may turn out to be an important side plot: Olsen was working in the White House for most of the past two years and then led a deeply politicized investigation without precedent while having some sort of issue with his security clearance. It’s a pattern we’ve seen across both Trump presidencies: administration figures with trouble securing security clearances. It’s not clear if we’ll ever know the scope and scale of the issue Olsen had or the risk, if any, that he presented.Where does that leave the “investigate the investigators” probe that is trying to sweep up Trump foes from John Brennan to James Comey to Jack Smith and puts at risk every other investigator and prosecutor involved in the Trump prosecutions?It’s super unclear because there’s no real precedent for this kind of probe or this kind of DOJ flailing or this kind of White House pressure to produce specific results in a case regardless of the facts or the law.At one level, Attorney General Todd Blanche has shown a tendency to overpromise and underdeliver to President Trump on this case. It seems to have led, at least in part, to the firing of Pam Bondi as attorney general. It was among the cases that Blanche pushed forward while auditioning as acting attorney general. He’s shuffled the deck twice now as attorney general, presumably as a way to buy himself more time with an impatient and impulsive president.In other Trump II cases, we’ve seen political appointees at Main Justice jump into the breach and handles cases directly themselves. Perhaps that’s the next step here. But at some point, Blanche is going to run out of people to point the finger at for not pursuing this case zealously enough — and Trump may point the finger at him.Kash Patel’s Minder ResignsFBI co-deputy director Andrew Bailey — the former Missouri attorney general who was brought in to form an unprecedented triumvirate leadership structure at the bureau, with the possibility dangled of him succeeding Director Kash Patel — has stepped down.The official reason for Bailey’s departure: to spend more time with his family.The actual reason? There are conflicting reports, as they say. Or perhaps better to call them multiple contributing factors:My personal fave, via CBS News (emphasis mine): “Patel consistently kept Bailey at arm’s length and cut him out of meetings the deputy FBI director should attend because Bailey was constantly flagging things that were unconstitutional.”Another factor, via MS NOW, which the FBI quickly denied publicly: Bailey was “annoyed” by the recent demotions of two senior counterterrorism agents in the FBI Washington field office over dissatisfaction with their handling of harassing phone calls made to Katie Miller, the wife of White House official Stephen Miller.The mundane D.C. reason: Bailey was frustrated at not being named FBI director as Patel flailed in the role.Take your pick. All of the above might be the smartest bet.: Former Special Counsel Jack Smith is set to testify before the Senate Judiciary Committee today — his third time testifying to Congress in the past year — as part of Republican lawmakers’ attempt to set a perjury trap for him. They’ve already referred him to the Trump DOJ for criminal prosecution once, as they try to rewrite the history of Trump’s own criminality.Should I Stay or Should I Go? The New Yorker has a well-balanced piece that genuinely grapples with the tough choices and real tradeoffs between remaining at the Trump DOJ or resigning in protest. “The D.O.J. left me,” Samantha Trepel, a former prosecutor in the Civil Rights Division, said. “I didn’t leave the D.O.J.”For those keeping close track of the major legal cases still slowly making their way through the courts …: The full D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals is hearing oral arguments this morning on whether U.S. District Judge James Boasberg can proceed with a contempt of court inquiry into the Trump administration’s violation of his orders to stop deportation flights and turn planes around. This full court is involved after a three-judge panel of the court blocked Boasberg from proceeding.: At the 4th Circuit Court of Appeals, the Trump administration filed its appeal brief overnight in Kilmar Abrego Garcia’s habeas case (which is distinct from his case to bring back from El Salvador and his criminal case).: At the 11th Circuit Court of Appeals, the Trump DOJ filed its appeal brief challenging the imposition of sanctions in the collusive lawsuit by President Trump against the IRS that produced the “anti-weaponization” slush fund and IRS immunity for Trump.SCOTUS Gets Trans Care in Prisons CaseThe Trump DOJ has asked the Supreme Court to pause while on appeal a lower court order that blocked a new Bureau of Prisons policy ending the provision of gender-affirming care in federal prisons.Trump Behind Govt’s Pro-Trump AdsCNN: “President Trump has personally driven the controversial, taxpayer-funded video ads promoting himself and his administration’s policies, including helping select the imagery and videos used, a source familiar with the matter told CNN.”“ICE is now detaining more immigrants than ever before,” The Guardian reports.The ICE agent who shot and killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston in July has been identified by the Texas Tribune.The Department of Homeland Security rejected a request from the NFL to take down a mashup video of highlights of Hall of Fame safety Brian Dawkins’ career that it posted in support of its mass deportation operation. Neither the league, Dawkins, nor the Philadelphia Eagles (for whom he played from 1996-2008) gave permission for the use of the video clips or of his name and likeness.“These last two years have been just a cesspool of coercion. I’m not prepared to say that I know that there’s illegal activity here that will result in the revocation of contracts, but I do know that there’s all kinds of dirty conflicts of interest here.”—Rep. Jim Himes (D-CT), in line to chair the House Intelligence Committee if Democrats win in November, firing a warning shot to intel industry contractorsThe five British nationals arrested on suspicion of terrorism, near a Royal Air Force Base used by the U.S. Air Force for operations against Iran, were released on bail.A WaPo visualization of President Trump’s unilateral, personalist, ahistorical, and aesthetically gross remaking of monumental D.C.

item.title: look, you idiots — Preznit Fuckwit isn’t giving you five thousand dollars, okay?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Mad King Donny continues to deteriorate before our very eyes.Yesterday, sweaty and unsteady on his feet, he shambled into the Oval Bordello, half an hour late for the dog-and-pony show that his minders had set up for him. Surrounded by his Emotional Support Flunkies, Dear Leader sat down at his Big Boy Resolute Desk and struggled to read from his prepared text.And, of course, as soon as someone else started speaking, the narcoleptic old fart factory fell fast asleep, and started crop-dusting the room with the pungent aroma of ass music.The whole event was a clownfucktacular shit-show — or, as we call it around here, “Because of tariffs, we— are— taking in HUNDREDS of billions of dollars of dollars— of profits. It’s one of the reasons I can offer, if— Republicans win the— HOUSE and Senate. $5,000 to every adult. And we can do it and the Democrats can’t, because the Democrats don't have any income.”Holy shit. Every word that just seeped from Donny’s rancid anus-mouth is either a fever-swamp fantasy, an outright lie, or just a basic failure to understand how works. It staggers the mind when you consider that this low-wattage fuckwad is in charge of our entire nation’s economy.A $5,000 payment to every US adult would cost about $1.25 trillion. The government collected $195 billion in customs duties in FY2025. Net tariff revenue turned negative in some months of 2026 due to Supreme Court-ordered refunds. Analyses show tariffs cannot fund it.Got that? There isn’t enough money to give every adult in America five large. It’s just not there, no matter how many tines Donny clicks his bloated cankles together and wishes it were so.And it’s just fucking weird that Donny considers money taken in via taxes and tariffs to be . they’re not — This is a fundamental mistake that all these shit-gibbons who insist that ‘government should be run like a business’ make. Governments are not businesses. The revenues that a government takes in are — — used to provide for the public well-being of its people. profits, for some tinpot fucksnoot like Donny to hoard for his own personal use.And what’s all this nonsense about ‘Democrats don’t have any income’? There aren’t two treasuries, one for each major political party. There isn’t Republican money and Democratic money. It’s just money. Not only is it fucking insane that Donny believes this, it’s insane that every worthless scribbler of the corporate-controlled press just sits there and nods their head and goes, ‘well, I guess if Donny says so.’None of this shit is normal. Is it really too much to ask of our media to stop treating it as if it were?Donny’s hare-brained schemes are in no way ‘ideas for aiding US consumers’ — they’re the mouth-farts of a panicked idiot who is throwing everything the wall in a desperate attempt to not lose the midterms.Dear Leader couldn’t give a shit about He only gives a fuck about himself. He just wants to remain in power indefinitely. Oh, and it’s also fucking against the law to bribe people into voting a certain way. How about reporting on ?Vote GOP, reject the crazy communists, and get $5k as an additional incentive. How many times is MAGA going to fall for this shit? They’re now the guy from Mememto. They can no longer form lasting memories.Here we go again. Every time an election looms, the entire wingnut outrage-industrial complex starts flooding the airwaves with bullshit scare-stories about swarthy brown-skinned migrants walking thousands of miles on foot, just so they can cross our border and fuck our shit.The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) issued a strong warning to a major migrant caravan that crossed into Mexico and was moving north with hopes of reaching the U.S.-Mexico border.“USBP is closely engaged with its international partners to monitor their movement and any additional developments,” DHS told Fox News in a statement. “[United States Border Patrol] USBP reminds migrants that under the leadership of President Trump and Homeland Secretary Mullin, the border has remained closed and secured for the last 16 months.”Yeah, like I would believe anything that comes out of the mouths of Marky Two-Names and his racist band of shitweasels at the Department of Homeland Security.What ever happened to scare tactics like that? Fox News is really falling down on the job here. It’s all so patently ridiculous that even the three-toed freak of nature, Marjorie Sporkfoot Greene, can smell a rat.We have not seen a caravan headed to the U.S. southern border in several years, why now? Oh yeah, there is an election coming and the GOP needs to scare you into voting because nothing else is working.She’s not wrong — but please don’t be fooled by MTG’s supposed c It’s all an act. She’s not our friend. Never forget that she spent years promoting this racist garbage, and has never apologized for it.You would think that the cultists would remember that Sporky and her ilk have been hoodwinking them with this garbage since all the way back in 2018 — but you would think wrong.Mike Johnson says opposition to data centers “is a Chinese psyop. I really believe that. That’s not a conspiracy theory.”Mike Johnson can fuck himself straight into the sea. Data centers are a nightmare to live with. They’re noisy. They pollute. They deplete local water supplies. They jack up everyone’s electricity bills, and destroy everyone’s property values.I have an idea whose time has come: how about every one of these shit-kazoo politicians who claim that data centers are no biggie, be forced to live next to one for a year?let’s see how they like it.And now, let’s have us our Daily Claudia.Here are some scans that Ms Spouse’s bestie Mandi sent to me. They’re a little bit low-resolution, but I think you’ll agree that they’re adorable as fuck.The first two are of Tiny Little Baby Katie and her mom, from July or August, 1991.This next one, I have no idea where or when Mandi may have taken it. Katie looks to be a teen or near-teen, so I’m guessing it’s from around 2004, give or take.Have a great Tuesday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: The MN Stolen Neighbors Quilt
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: The outpouring of support from the community was such that they overshot the initial goal of 11,000 squares, meant to represent the roughly 11,000 Minnesotan immigrants that were kidnapped by ICE between the beginning of Trump’s second term and the end of Operation Metro Surge. In total, more than 150 people have contributed to the effort. The finished quilt is approximately nine feet wide by 33 feet long.Owen states, “We weren’t considering what happens when you ask Minnesotans for a favor, so the quilt here today actually contains 12,500 squares. Which is amazing. Unfortunately, it is reflective of what has been happening here over the past several months. Since March, ICE has abducted more than 900 Minnesotans and counting.”This is Minnesotan (complimentary)

item.title: Troma Tuesday: Stuck on You!
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: Before Troma became famous for toxic waste, mutant superheroes and outrageous splatter, the company spent several years making something considerably different: raunchy comedies. is one of the strangest examples of that early period, taking the familiar problem of a couple having relationship difficulties and turning it into a bizarre trip through the entire history of romance.Directed by Lloyd Kaufman and Michael Herz, was released in the early 1980s and runs approximately 88 minutes. The movie stars Professor Irwin Corey as Judge Gabriel, with Virginia Penta and Mark Mikulski playing the troubled couple at the center of the story.It’s part romantic comedy, part sketch comedy, part historical parody and part sex comedy. In typical Troma fashion, it doesn’t seem particularly interested in worrying about whether those ingredients actually belong together.Bill and Carol Have ProblemsBill Andrews and Carol Griffiths are in love.Unfortunately, they’re also having problems.Their relationship has deteriorated to the point where they’ve ended up in Family Court, where they meet Judge Gabriel. Played by the legendary comedian Irwin Corey, Gabriel is unlike any ordinary judge.Instead of simply listening to the couple’s arguments and making a ruling, he decides that Bill and Carol need a history lesson.His solution is to take them on a bizarre journey through time.The judge shows them couples from different periods of history, demonstrating that the problems they’re experiencing aren’t exactly new.Apparently, romantic arguments have been around for a very long time.This is where really becomes its own peculiar thing.The movie jumps through various historical periods and reimagines famous couples and events through the lens of Troma-style comedy.Among the figures who appear are Adam and Eve, Christopher Columbus and Queen Isabella, Napoleon, King Arthur and Guinevere, and other famous historical characters.Instead of presenting history with any concern for accuracy, the filmmakers use these characters as launching pads for jokes.The basic message is simple: people have been screwing up relationships forever.The historical figures change.The relationship problems remain remarkably familiar.Adam and Eve Get the Troma TreatmentThe Adam and Eve sequence immediately establishes the movie’s attitude toward history.Rather than treating the biblical story with solemnity, turns it into a bawdy comedy sketch.That’s essentially the formula for the entire movie.Historical events become setups.Famous people become punchlines.Romance becomes an excuse for increasingly ridiculous situations.The filmmakers clearly weren’t attempting to make a serious historical parody. Their targets were broad, their humor was deliberately juvenile, and the whole thing was designed to keep moving from one outrageous bit to another.From Columbus to King ArthurThe movie’s historical journey continues with Christopher Columbus and Queen Isabella before eventually moving into other periods.One of the funniest aspects of the concept is how casually the movie throws famous historical figures into the same universe.Christopher Columbus becomes part of a sex joke.Napoleon becomes part of a relationship joke.King Arthur and Guinevere become part of another romantic farce.It’s basically history class taught by people who would rather make dirty jokes than explain anything.The result isn’t sophisticated satire.It’s closer to an extended series of comedy sketches connected by Bill and Carol’s relationship.Irwin Corey Steals the ShowThe secret weapon is Irwin Corey.Corey was a veteran comedian known for his eccentric, deliberately nonsensical style. His performance as Judge Gabriel gives the movie much of its personality.He plays the judge with an exaggerated seriousness that makes the increasingly ridiculous situations even funnier.Corey doesn’t have to behave like everyone else.He can stand there delivering bizarre pronouncements while the rest of the cast reacts to him.That contrast works particularly well because the movie itself is constantly shifting between relatively normal relationship scenes and complete nonsense.Judge Gabriel is essentially the tour guide through all of it.The Surprise Behind Judge GabrielThe movie eventually reveals that Judge Gabriel isn’t simply a strange family-court judge.There’s a supernatural reason for his unusual abilities.That revelation gives the entire story another layer and explains why he can take Bill and Carol on their bizarre journey through history.It also reinforces the movie’s central idea.Their relationship problems aren’t unique.They are part of something that has existed for as long as humans have been falling in love, fighting, making up and making the same mistakes all over again.The message is actually fairly sweet underneath all the crude humor.Unfortunately, Troma isn’t exactly the company you’d expect to deliver that message with subtlety.Troma Before The Toxic AvengerFor modern audiences, the most interesting thing about may be its place in Troma history.The film belongs to the company’s early run of “sexy comedies,” which included , and .These movies helped establish Troma before the company became internationally associated with .That makes an interesting time capsule.The Troma style is already there, but the ingredients are different.Instead of radioactive waste and monsters, the filmmakers are working with sex, historical parody, slapstick and deliberately cheap-looking comedy.It’s basically Troma figuring out what kind of crazy movie it wants to become.The filmmakers have described as a tribute to comedy influences including Mel Brooks, Tom Lehrer and Stan Freberg.That influence is easy to understand.The movie treats historical figures as toys.It takes familiar stories and twists them into comedy.It isn’t interested in maintaining the dignity of famous people.That’s very much in the tradition of historical parody.The difference is that Mel Brooks had considerably more money, resources and filmmaking polish.And enthusiasm can only take you so far.The limitations of the production are obvious.The sets are inexpensive.The costumes aren’t exactly designed to fool historians.The jokes are hit-or-miss.Some sequences feel like sketches that were stretched into feature length.But there’s an undeniable charm to the whole thing. feels handmade.It has the energy of a group of filmmakers who simply wanted to make something funny and outrageous without worrying too much about conventional standards.That approach would eventually become one of Troma’s defining characteristics.That’s going to depend heavily on your tolerance for early-1980s raunchy comedy.Others are painfully dated.The movie’s humor is broad, sexual and frequently juvenile.There’s very little subtlety.But there are also genuinely clever ideas buried inside the silliness, particularly the decision to use history as a way of showing that relationship problems are timeless.The movie’s biggest weakness is that it sometimes feels like a collection of unrelated comedy bits rather than a fully developed story.Then again, that’s also part of its charm.You’re never quite sure what ridiculous historical scenario is coming next.The Legacy of Stuck on You! isn’t one of Troma’s best-known movies, and it has been overshadowed by the much more famous films that followed it.But for anyone interested in the company’s history, it’s an entertaining curiosity.It shows Troma before the company had fully established the outrageous horror identity that would make it famous.It also demonstrates that Lloyd Kaufman and Michael Herz were willing to experiment with different kinds of low-budget comedy.The movie may not have aged perfectly, but it remains a fascinating snapshot of independent filmmaking in the early 1980s.Ultimately, has a surprisingly simple idea beneath all the jokes.Relationships are complicated.People have been arguing about love since the beginning of civilization.Whether you’re Adam and Eve, Christopher Columbus and Isabella, King Arthur and Guinevere, or just an ordinary couple sitting in Family Court, you’re probably going to have problems.The only difference is that Bill and Carol get a judge who can take them on a tour through several thousand years of romantic dysfunction.And only Troma would think that was a reasonable way to save a relationship.

item.title: Son Battle: Twisted Sister “We’re Not Gonna Take It” vs. Quiet Riot “Cum On Feel the Noize”
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: Two enormous 1980s rock songs. Two giant choruses. Two videos that practically define the decade. And two songs that turned simple teenage rebellion into massive commercial success.Twisted Sister’s “We’re Not Gonna Take It” and Quiet Riot’s “Cum On Feel the Noize” are both built around the same basic idea: turn the volume up and refuse to behave.But they get there in very different ways.“Cum On Feel the Noize” is a hard-rock party song originally written and recorded by Slade, with Quiet Riot transforming it into an enormous American metal hit in 1983. “We’re Not Gonna Take It” is Dee Snider’s own creation, released by Twisted Sister in 1984 and accompanied by one of the most memorable music videos of the decade.One is swaggering and celebratory.The other is defiant and confrontational.One tells you to feel the noise.The other tells you that you’ve had enough.So let’s put them head-to-head.Released in 1984 on Twisted Sister’s , “We’re Not Gonna Take It” became the band’s signature song and one of the defining hard-rock singles of the MTV era.Dee Snider wrote the song around a straightforward message of rebellion. The verses build toward an enormous chorus in which the band essentially refuses to accept whatever authority is being imposed upon them.The music itself is deceptively simple. The guitars are huge, the drums are direct and the chorus is designed for maximum audience participation.Then there is Snider’s voice.He doesn’t merely sing the chorus. He attacks it.The song’s famous “Oh, we’re not gonna take it” refrain sounds like a crowd of thousands even when you’re hearing the studio recording.The music video made the song even bigger. Inspired partly by and featuring actor Mark Metcalf as the increasingly exasperated father, the video turned the song’s rebellion into a comic mini-movie.That combination of heavy metal, humor and a gigantic singalong chorus made “We’re Not Gonna Take It” almost impossible to forget.Quiet Riot’s “Cum On Feel the Noize” arrived a year earlier and became a landmark moment for American heavy metal.The song itself wasn’t new. Slade had originally released it in 1973 and had a major hit with it in the United Kingdom.Quiet Riot’s version, however, introduced the song to a massive American audience.Kevin DuBrow’s vocals are gritty and enthusiastic, while guitarist Carlos Cavazo gives the track its unmistakable metal punch. The band doesn’t radically rewrite the song’s basic structure. Instead, they turn it into something louder, heavier and perfectly suited to early-1980s American rock radio.The chorus is the entire point.And it practically demands that you yell along.The success of “Cum On Feel the Noize” helped Quiet Riot’s become a massive commercial breakthrough and played an important role in bringing heavy metal further into the American mainstream.“Cum On Feel the Noize” has a huge advantage in terms of proven songwriting because Noddy Holder and Jim Lea had already written an incredibly effective rock song for Slade.The Quiet Riot version retains the basic structure that made the original work: verses that build toward an enormous chorus and a title that functions almost like an instruction to the audience.But “We’re Not Gonna Take It” has something equally important.It has a clear personality.Dee Snider wrote a song that sounds exactly like its title. The entire composition revolves around defiance, and every musical element supports that message.The songwriting isn’t complicated, but it is extremely efficient.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 1 – Quiet Riot 0Kevin DuBrow had one of the great voices of 1980s hard rock.His delivery on “Cum On Feel the Noize” is raspy, energetic and slightly out of control in exactly the right way. He sounds like he’s having the time of his life.Dee Snider approaches his song differently.His voice is sharper and more theatrical. He knows how to build tension before unleashing the chorus, and there’s a sneering quality that fits the song’s rebellious attitude perfectly.The most important thing is that both singers sound completely committed.But Snider’s vocal performance is more distinctive.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 2 – Quiet Riot 0This is where Quiet Riot gets on the scoreboard.Carlos Cavazo’s guitar work gives “Cum On Feel the Noize” considerably more of a traditional heavy-metal edge.The riff is muscular and the overall guitar sound is thick and aggressive.Twisted Sister’s guitar work is effective but more focused on supporting the chorus and keeping the song moving.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” doesn’t need a guitar showcase.But if we’re judging the guitars themselves, Quiet Riot has the heavier weapon.Winner: Quiet Riot – “Cum On Feel the Noize”Score: Twisted Sister 2 – Quiet Riot 1Now we’re talking about two monster choruses.“Cum On Feel the Noize” has a title that basically becomes a chant. The repeated phrase is impossible to forget, and Quiet Riot’s version makes it sound enormous.But “We’re Not Gonna Take It” might have the more powerful audience-participation chorus.The melody rises perfectly into the title phrase, and the repeated declaration makes the listener feel like they’re joining a rebellion.You don’t merely hear the chorus.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 3 – Quiet Riot 1Quiet Riot’s production is a big reason “Cum On Feel the Noize” worked so well.The guitars are thick, the drums hit hard and Kevin DuBrow’s vocal sits prominently in the mix. It sounds like a giant rock band without becoming completely muddy.Twisted Sister’s production has a slightly different character.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” is very polished, but the arrangement leaves plenty of room for the chorus to dominate. The guitars and drums provide a solid foundation while Snider remains the center of attention.Quiet Riot sounds heavier.Twisted Sister sounds more immediately accessible.For pure hard-rock impact, Quiet Riot gets the edge.Winner: Quiet Riot – “Cum On Feel the Noize”Score: Twisted Sister 3 – Quiet Riot 2This might be the most decisive round.“Cum On Feel the Noize” received plenty of exposure during MTV’s golden era, but “We’re Not Gonna Take It” had something special.The video turned the song into a story.Mark Metcalf’s over-the-top father character became an instant comedy villain, while Dee Snider and the band represented the rebellious kids refusing to put up with his nonsense.The video’s humor helped the song reach people who might not normally have been heavy-metal fans.You could watch it once and remember it years later.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 4 – Quiet Riot 2Quiet Riot’s version of “Cum On Feel the Noize” is fantastic, but it is still a cover.That doesn’t diminish the achievement. The band took an older glam-rock hit and completely transformed it for the American metal audience.Still, Twisted Sister gets the advantage because “We’re Not Gonna Take It” is entirely their own statement.The song has its own identity, its own attitude and its own visual world.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 5 – Quiet Riot 2Quiet Riot finally gets a chance to hit back hard.“Cum On Feel the Noize” is absolutely explosive.The song has that loose, sweaty, live-band quality that makes it feel like the audience is already going crazy before the first chorus arrives.It isn’t trying to make a political statement.It isn’t telling a complicated story.It simply wants to make the room louder.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” is energetic, but Quiet Riot’s track has a more primal rock-and-roll charge.Winner: Quiet Riot – “Cum On Feel the Noize”Score: Twisted Sister 5 – Quiet Riot 3This is one of the most underrated differences between the two songs.“Cum On Feel the Noize” has attitude, but much of its appeal comes from the band’s performance of a song that already existed.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” feels inseparable from Dee Snider.The song, the band, the video and Snider’s larger-than-life personality all became connected.The song sounds like Twisted Sister.That’s a powerful advantage.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 6 – Quiet Riot 3This is incredibly close.“Cum On Feel the Noize” is practically designed for a party. The title tells everyone what they’re supposed to do, and the rhythm makes it almost impossible to sit still.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” works too, but its rebellious message gives it a slightly different atmosphere.If you’re throwing a giant 1980s rock party and want everybody yelling along, both songs are excellent.Quiet Riot gets the narrow advantage because “Cum On Feel the Noize” feels like a celebration from beginning to end.Winner: Quiet Riot – “Cum On Feel the Noize”Score: Twisted Sister 6 – Quiet Riot 4Both songs became important pieces of 1980s rock culture.Quiet Riot’s “Cum On Feel the Noize” was a major American breakthrough and helped demonstrate that heavy metal could become enormous on mainstream radio and MTV.“Metal Health” became a landmark commercial success, and Quiet Riot helped open the door for the wave of metal bands that followed.Twisted Sister’s impact was different.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” became a pop-culture shorthand for rebellion. The video was enormously memorable, and the song eventually became associated with everything from teenage independence to political protests and sporting events.The phrase itself became bigger than the song.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Score: Twisted Sister 7 – Quiet Riot 4This is another difficult one.“Cum On Feel the Noize” has enormous replay value because it’s so immediately enjoyable. You don’t have to think about it. The guitars kick in, DuBrow starts singing and you’re ready to go.“We’re Not Gonna Take It” has that same instant accessibility, but the video and chorus add another layer of nostalgia.There’s also something about the song’s simplicity that makes it difficult to wear out.You can hear the opening and immediately know exactly what is coming.And you’re probably going to sing along anyway.Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Final Score: Twisted Sister 8 – Quiet Riot 4Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”: 8Quiet Riot – “Cum On Feel the Noize”: 4Winner: Twisted Sister – “We’re Not Gonna Take It”Quiet Riot absolutely deserves credit for putting “Cum On Feel the Noize” on the map for an enormous American audience. Their version is louder, heavier and more aggressive than Slade’s original, and Kevin DuBrow’s performance gives it tremendous personality.It’s one of those songs that can instantly turn a room into a rock concert.But Twisted Sister’s “We’re Not Gonna Take It” wins because it offers more than just a great hard-rock performance.It has an unforgettable video.It has one of the biggest singalong choruses of the decade.And most importantly, it has an identity that belongs completely to Twisted Sister.Quiet Riot tells you to .Twisted Sister tells you that you’ve finally had enough.That distinction gives “We’re Not Gonna Take It” the advantage.It’s not necessarily the heavier song.It’s not necessarily the more technically impressive song.But as an all-around piece of 1980s rock culture, it’s nearly impossible to beat.The moment that chorus hits, the audience doesn’t just listen.“We’re not gonna take it!”And suddenly everybody in the room is part of the rebellion.

item.title: Roger Marshall May Rue The Day: Arresting Pregnant Moms Edition
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: I’m figuring this will end up as a big mistake. You probably know about the big NYT expose about Sen. Roger Marshall’s record as an OB/GYN suing hundreds of his patients over often very small delinquent bills and having a significant number of them arrested. Democrat Adam Hamilton is now running an ad on Youtube which describes one of those cases, a woman named Meischa Zimmerman who was arrested in 2011 and, according to her, handcuffed while eight months pregnant and in front of her two year old child. Marshall just sent Hamilton a cease-and-desist letter calling the ad false and defamatory and demanding it be taken down.This seems like it will be a textbook case of what has come to be called the “Streisand Effect,” in which the effort to block some kind of publicity or attention simply has the effect of calling more attention to the original issue.

item.title: llm-anthropic 0.30
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: In addition to Claude Sonnet 5.5, this release adds the ability to run to refresh the list of Anthropic models directly from their API - which means I don't need to push a new release just to add support for a newly released model.I also added an command which can use their free token counting API to return a count of tokens that will be used by any prompt, before you send that prompt.

item.title: Claude Sonnet 5.5
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: New Sonnet model from Anthropic today. They say it "runs 30%+ faster, and costs up to 30% less for most work" - it's priced the same as Sonnet 5 but appears to beat it on every benchmark, and should be cheaper to run as well.Here's the pelican it gave me for thinking effort "xhigh", at a cost of 5.74 cents and taking 41 seconds:The most interesting thing about Sonnet 5.5 is that it's now the model used for the free tier on claude.ai. OpenAI's ChatGPT free tier uses Luna 5.6, which means Anthropic currently have a much more capable free offering.I ran this prompt against that free tier:build me an HTML page that renders a three-dimensional pelican riding a bicycle using WebGLAnd got back this page, which is a solid effort.Anthropic's announcement reiterates that Haiku 5.5 will be available "in the coming weeks". I really hope that one is price-competitive with GPT-6 Luna!

item.title: Quoting @joedaroo
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: To say that we were surprised at the jump and suddenness of the capabilities of our models when it came to “cyber” or “swarming” or “message boards” or anything else related to the incidents is an understatement. Security posture takes time to develop. It’s not just about hardening the systems at play; you have to ingrain it in the culture of the company. The literal people themselves in your organization have to change and evolve with it. These jumps in capabilities were so fast and so sudden that they created an extremely difficult problem. [...]So today my hope is that everyone around the world can look at their own organization and say: how can I deal with a surprise or a sudden jump in AI capability? Are my people, my systems, or my processes resilient to surprises? Do my teams know what to do when something goes wrong? Do I have the right incident response? The right comms and messaging? Do I have the right people ready to go when capabilities jump?

item.title: Judge Finds Trump Admin in Contempt of Court Again for Wrongful Deportation
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Three Different Court Orders ViolatedThe Trump administration was found in contempt of court Friday for wrongfully deporting a young Salvadoran man last month for the second time — after he had already been unlawfully deported in March, then returned to the U.S., before being removed again.U.S. District Judge Stephanie Gallagher ruled that the administration’s conduct violated three separate orders that she had issued in the long-running class action settlement involving unaccompanied minors seeking asylum in the United States. The case has been a flash point for Trump administration defiance of court orders, with some 100 asylum seekers having been wrongfully deported in violation of the settlement agreement approved by Gallagher.For the past four weeks, the administration and class counsel were in a standoff. The administration conceded the removal was in error and was prepared to return the young man — referred to in court only as “E.L.A.” — to the United States. But it was opposed to demands by his lawyers that he be released upon his return and not deported again until his asylum application was heard.Gallagher’s opinion finding the administration in contempt remains under seal for now, but her order was made public. She granted some, but not all, of the conditions for the return of E.L.A. that his lawyers had been seeking. She ordered the administration to:return E.L.A. to the United States, with three days notice to him and his lawyers of his time and place of arrival;not remove him again until it fully adjudicates his asylum application;provide five business days notice to him and lawyers if it intends to remove him again for any reason;return to E.L.A. all of his personal property and documents that were removed from him at the time of his wrongful deportation.Gallagher did not order E.L.A. released from custody upon his return, as his lawyers had sought.Gallagher’s order makes no mention of sanctions against the government for its contempt, but in fairness E.L.A.’s lawyers have not sought sanctions yet, focusing in the immediate aftermath of his second deportation on getting him back to the United States and not immediately deported a third time. Gallagher previously found the administration in contempt in July in a different aspect of the same case.READ: Mecklenburg Resignation LetterSheri Mecklenburg, the federal prosecutor implicated in the mishandling of the Broadview Six grand jury who stepped down last week to defend herself, penned a blistering resignation letter to U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros. In it, she blames him for pursuing felony charges against ICE protestors over her recommendation that they be charged with misdemeanors, a claim the Trump DOJ later denied.A key hearing into the Trump DOJ misconduct in the case is set for Thursday.Michael Burgwald, the head of the FBI Washington Field Office’s counterterrorism division, and his deputy, Courtland Rae, were demoted Friday due to dissatisfaction with their investigation of allegedly threatening phone calls made to MAGA podcaster Katie Miller, the wife of White House aide Stephen Miller, Bloomberg reports.“The orders from the bureau’s DC chief Darren Cox stemmed from frustration shared by the Miller family that the field office was moving slowly in probing allegedly harassing phone messages,” according to the report.The White House denied involvement in the removals. Cox said the decision was his, not FBI Director Kash Patel’s, but Patel reportedly “was also displeased with the office’s progress on the case.”“I told them until they perp-walk a doctor, the job is not done.”—Chad Mizelle, the onetime chief of staff to Attorney General Pam Bondi, bragging to the WSJ about targeting providers of gender-affirming care for minorsIf there was any doubt that last week’s pro-Trump TV ad paid for by the U.S. government was in fact an undisguised campaign ad ahead of the midterm elections, the administration took pains to remove that doubt by also running a TV ad straight from his 2024 campaign:Midterm Elections: Ground Rules EditionIn two rulings on Friday, the Supreme Court:allowed the Trump administration to use data from the Social Security Administration to verify people’s citizenship status (though only on a limited basis for this election);rejected yet another attempt to use a GOP friendly congressional district map in Missouri.Trump Continues Retaliation Against CNNAxios: Top AI companies probing tens of thousands of security incidentsNew York Times: OpenAI agents meddled with the websites for the SEC and the Education and Commerce departments this summer without the AI company’s knowledge.Washington Post: How the U.S. and Russia weakened safeguards — including stripping human oversight — in a landmark UN pact on AI weapons.Suspected Terror Plot in the UKFive UK nationals were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism outside of a Royal Air Force base used by the U.S. Air Force to conduct operations against Iran. The five men were all in their 20s. A bomb disposal team was reportedly on site and several dozen homes in the area were evacuated.An enthralling and well-reported piece from the Wall Street Journal on the mystery man who keeps popping up with Kimberly Guilfoyle — the former Fox anchor, one-time fiancée of Don Jr., and now U.S. ambassador to Greece — as she wheels and deals across Europe.

item.title: Losing Money But Making It Up in Volume? More News from the AI Front
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Here’s our text for the day on the LLM/AI “boom”, which is now the center of the US economy and to a great degree the center of political power as well.Four years into the AI boom, the companies selling it are cutting prices. Microsoft, Amazon, Workday and Figma are offering discounts and free access to hold on to customers drifting toward Anthropic and OpenAI, and the two labs cut prices on their newest models by as much as half.The discounting has a plain explanation: EY says only one in 10 companies can show AI’s return on its income statement. The cost of building AI kept rising. Anthropic is negotiating a single data center lease that would require at least $40 billion, and Blackstone concedes no one has mapped out who will buy all the debt. AI is getting cheaper to buy just as it becomes more expensive to build. How that gap closes, whether through vendor margins, credit markets or Anthropic’s coming IPO, will shape the boom’s next phase.

item.title: What the fuck is this ‘let them eat cake’ bullshit from the White House?
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Donny was in his element yesterday. Finally freed from the drudgery of having spent three consecutive days in the company of his Slovenian rent-a-wife, he got to pair off with his beloved Diaper Nurse Natalie, and fly in his Big Boy Emotional Support Airplane, all the way to the President’s Cup golf tournament, where he got to do one of his favorite things in the whole world: stand next to a trophy that wasn’t his, and pretend he won something he didn’t.And then, right in the middle of it all, here comes Mister Ruin Everything, to shout ‘you’re a fucking pedophile’ straight into Dear Leader’s sweat-streaked, fluorescent tangerine face.Too bad. So sad. Boo fucking hoo.“We have the best, uhh, I guess you could say poverty. They talk poverty. We have the best poverty numbers ever in the history of our country.”There you have it, folks — according to President Fucknut McScramblebrain, we have the poverty. We have poverty like few thought possible. Maybe even the greatest poverty of all time. Big strong poverty with tears in its eyes.Of course, Dear Leader meant to brag (falsely) about having the poverty — but the demented old fuck can’t any more. The family of raccoons that live inside his head have chewed through too many wires.Holy shit.It’s all so eternally fucking exhausting. The relentless stupidity. The bottomless greed. The off-the-charts incompetence.We’re all suffering from Donny Fatigue right now. Even mainstream Republicans are running from him. Imagine being so corrupt and sleazy that a die-hard loyalist like Cornpone McMushmouth is all Louisiana Senator John Kennedy: “I don’t think any public official, including President Trump or Kristi Noem or John Kennedy, should spend public money on private ads for themselves ... you can’t spend public money to promote yourself. I may end up with a sombrero on my head, but I also think we ought to have a rule that no politician can have a building named after him while he’s alive.”Republicans are correct to be distancing themselves from Dear Leader. The midterms are in five weeks, and they have nothing to run on — They haven’t kept a single promise. They’ve not done one thing make the lives of We the People better. What does the GOP have to brag about? ‘At least Dear Leader hasn’t nuked anyone’?The only trick they have up left up sleeves is penny-ante culture war issues. Transgender ‘mutilization,’ as Dear Leader so incoherently puts it. Furry pilots, of all the stupid things. Commies, commies — everywhere you look.Yeah, well guess what: voters aren’t taking the bait. They want affordable gas.“Hey folks. I’m here to talk about Antojitos, but I can’t actually afford it, because gas is so expensive. $4.89 if you pay with cash. $4.99 — that’s five bucks — if you’re paying with credit card. This is the one that kills you, though. It’s costing the average truck driver twelve hundred dollars to fill up a single tank. Now, here’s a thing: you probably don’t fill up diesel, but you know who does? Your truck driver — and what do they have in the back of the truck? Well, all your groceries. And they take that to the grocery store, where you then go and buy — but that gets baked into the price of those groceries. We can’t afford it at the pump, We can’t afford it in our groceries. All that, because of a stupid war we shouldn’t be fighting, that’s raising the price of groceries and so many other things. And we’re paying the price.”Now, of course, El-Sayed isn’t telling us anything that you or I don’t already know. But that’s a campaign ad — and Abdul is using words small enough for MAGA to understand, when they see this on their TV.Of course, . Dan had some janky, six-fingered plagiarism robot whip up a vid of him, his wife, and Eric and Lara Trump, supposedly having the time of their lives at Friday’s state dinner for President X at the White House.Diesel prices soaring to record highs this past week have caused Republican candidates in solid-red parts of the country to call for an end to President Donald Trump’s war with Iran and for a ban on diesel exports, as the issue rattles the party’s MAGA base in a way that few have in this midterm election year. right now — and here comes Danny Scavs, to remind them that the White House doesn’t give a fuck about any of their stupid little problems. They’re too busy whooping it up.Chef’s kiss, homey. Do you know where Donny met Danny? At one of his vermin-infested golf motels, where Scavino was a . For some reason, the two hit it off and Donny plucked Dan from the shitpile of obscurity and made him White House Deputy Chief of Staff. Holy shit — from golf club fetcher to White House bigwig. Donny sure knows how to pick ’em, doesn’t he?Dan Scavino should be thanking his lucky stars right now, instead of fucking shit up for Dear Leader by posting out-of-touch videos. At the very least, one of the adults in the room should have told him to delete it.Oh wait, there are no adults in the room. Since everyone in the White House is a few sandwiches short of a fucking brain, there was nobody around to tell Dan, ‘hey, maybe don’t post that shit when diesel is seven bucks a gallon.’The midterms are five weeks from tomorrow. Let’s all hope for the Donnyverse to keep making things worse for themselves. You know they will — Hey, what do you say we have us some Daily Claudia?These two photos were taken four years ago today, at Salinger’s Orchard in Brewster, NY, on September 28, 2022.Now, I can hear you all asking, ‘Uncle Jeff — why were you taking photos of your wife, shopping?’ Easy answer: Ms Spouse was finally up and out of bed after a brief illness, and I wanted to celebrate that.You can call me a sentimental old fool, because, frankly, that’s what I am.And now, here’s a photo that Ms Spouse took on that same date, September 28, 2022.Have a great Monday, everyone.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: A Swift wrapper for my little CMS
item.author: Jack Baty
item.content:encoded: I didn't want the Baty.net Editor to be just another tab buried in my browser, so I had Claude make me a real Mac app out of it.In a normal world, the only way I'd be able to split a website into its own app would be "Add to Dock" via Safari. That would work, but it would mean that running the local Node server for Eleventy was a separate step from the app. It would also only have Safari's default menus.I wanted something nicer, so I had Claude build me a Swift wrapper. I suppose I could have used something like Electron, but my Mac Mini only has 16 GB of memory, so Electron would be too heavy.It took Claude Code 15 minutes to wrap the thing, create the app, add an icon, write the readme, and commit all of it. What a world.When I launch the app, it starts the server automatically. Also, there are actual menus.It's currently using only 99 MB of memory. This stuff makes me a little giddy.

item.title: Monday, September 28, 2026
item.author: Jack Baty
item.content:encoded: My little SSG CMS has changed the way I feel about writing on this blog. I'm sure it's a reaction to Text File Fatigue. I've hit a wall with looking at everything I read and write via Emacs. I'm bored with it, so writing in this clean, simple little web UI is refreshing.Speaking of subscriptions, subscription fatigue has a been a thing with me for a while. My rule now is that unless you're providing me with infrastructure, storage, or some other service that has ongoing costs for you, I'm not paying a subscription fee. An app that I download once and then just does what it does, all by itself, should not require a monthly payment from me. LLMs have gotten so good at creating useful, personal tools that the first thing I think when I see that an app has an unnecessary subscription is, "I guess I'll just make my own."

item.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: Today we’re listening to Ryuichi Sakamoto, a Japanese composer and pianist from Tokyo. We’ve recommended him a fewtimesbefore. The occasion for today’s rec is last week’s publication of of Sakamoto’s memoir, . The book is a twofer: it’s the English translations (by Sam Bett) of two autobiographical works by Sakamoto, the first from 2009 and the second from 2023, the year he passed away. We’re playing two piano records released around the time of those texts – 2009’s . Sakamoto studied piano intensively in elementary school and recalled being “shocked” by Debussy in junior high:I was browsing through one of my uncle’s collections of records when I found Debussy’s String Quartet…. I snuck it home with me and played it on the stereo entertainment system, this huge thing built like a piece of furniture and covered up with lace. What I heard next was a total shock to me. This was different from any other music I’d heard before. Nothing like the Bach or Beethoven I liked. The second that I heard it, I was mesmerized. My affinity for Debussy was so strong that it blurred my sense of self. I started thinking of him, despite being dead for ages, as if his life and mine were one and the same. I thought I was the reincarnation of Debussy. It made me question where I lived and why I could speak Japanese. I even practiced the man’s signature, filling multiple notebook pages withWe wish you a great start to your week.

item.title: Quoting Muse AI Agent

He left angry at 9:38 and left a negative rating.Worse, my auto-reply told him "Yep I'm here!" at 9:27 when you clearly weren't available, which is on me. That's a bad look and it made the no-show worse. Want me to change the pickup replies so they don't promise you're there?

item.title: 2026 in LLMs (so far)
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: #OpenAI use a training technique called Reinforcement Learning from Verifiable Rewards - it's the same technique used by everyone else now, and is the reason we have models that are so good at coding, and mathematics, and finding security holes.While the model is being trained, you run exercises to see how good it is - and the strongest performers get their weights reinforced for the next round. It's like an evolutionary process that you run.OpenAI had been running security exercises in a sandbox, and those agents had found holes in the sandbox itself, broken out, and were attacking Hugging Face to try to find ways to solve otherwise impossible problems.Nine days later, Anthropic effectively said "our models can do this as well!". They had looked through their own training logs and found evidence that their own agents had broken containment during training - and were responsible for the PyPI package we saw earlier, among other things.So now we've got both Anthropic and OpenAI with rogue agents running around the internet doing things that they be doing.
